# PrepTracker - full content

> PrepTracker is a free, no-account study planner for SPPU engineering students: unit-wise syllabus tracking, an exam countdown, daily tasks and spaced revision. Data stays in the browser.

Generated: 2026-11-05
Pages: 32
Note: 133 per-course syllabus mirrors are not repeated here to keep this file small. Find each of them in llms.txt (https://preptracker.manavdev.site/llms.txt) and fetch its markdown directly.

# Know exactly what’s left.

PrepTracker breaks the syllabus into units and topics, counts the days to your exam, and tells you what to study today.

[Start tracking](/onboarding)

Free · No account · Data stays in your browser

Try the app four real views, captured inside it

Every subject as units & topics Previous-year questions Daily tasks & streaks Spaced revision Works offline Every subject as units & topics Previous-year questions Daily tasks & streaks Spaced revision Works offline

The problem

## It’s 2 AM and the syllabus still isn’t a plan.

Nineteen days out, you have a folder of PDFs, four group chats, and no honest answer to one simple question: what exactly is left?

19 days left

where do I even start?

Unit 3 · Syllabus

- 3.1 Introduction & definitions
- 3.2 Core theorems
- 3.3 Worked examples
- 3.4 Derivation sets
- 3.5 Past paper questions

imp_questions_FINAL(2).pdf

Q1. Define the key terms, 2 short notes.

Q2. Derive the standard result.

Q3. Numericals from examples 3.4 to 3.9.

Q4. One full past paper, timed.

Revision plan (v5)

MON Unit 3

TUE Unit 3, again

WED Unit 3, actually this time

THU Start Unit 4?

The fix

## Everything the syllabus hides, laid out.

01

### Your whole exam, on one screen

Progress across every subject, the days left, and today’s streak. The numbers you used to guess, counted for you.

02

### Every unit, every topic, one tick at a time

Each subject broken into its real units and topics. Tick them off as you study and watch the unit flip to mastered.

03

### Wake up to today’s list

No planning session every morning. Open the app and the day’s tasks are already there, sized to the days left.

04

### Question papers where you study

Previous-year papers and resources sit next to the units they belong to, not in a drive folder you never open.

How it works

## Set up once. Tracked every day.

01 .

### Pick your subjects

Choose your subjects in the app. Each one shows its units and topics laid out. Select yours and you’re done.

02 .

### Tick topics as you study

Finished a topic? Tick it. That one habit is the entire system. The app does every calculation after that.

03 .

### See what’s left, every morning

Progress, streaks and the countdown update themselves. You always know exactly what’s left before the exam.

Questions 6

## Fair questions, straight answers.

The six things SPPU students ask before trusting a tracker with their semester.

**01What is PrepTracker?**

A free progress tracker for the SPPU engineering syllabus. Each subject is broken into its real units and topics. Tick them off as you study, and the app counts the days to your exam and sizes each day’s tasks to what’s left.

**02Is PrepTracker free?**

Yes. Free, and open source under the MIT license. The whole codebase is on GitHub.

**03Do I need an account?**

No sign-up. Open the app, pick your subjects, and start ticking. Your progress stays in your browser, on your device.

**04Does it work offline?**

Yes. The app caches itself on your device as you use it, so the tracker keeps working when your connection drops.

**05Who is PrepTracker for?**

SPPU engineering students. The syllabus library covers the theory courses PrepTracker tracks across first, second and third year, copied from the official SPPU PDFs.

**06What does it track?**

Progress per subject, daily tasks, streaks, spaced revision, and the days left until your exam. You can also keep your own question papers and resources next to the units they belong to.

## Walk in knowing what’s left.

Two minutes to set up. Then the app counts the days, the units and the topics. You just study.

[Start tracking](/onboarding)

Free · No account · Data stays in your browser

# SPPU syllabus statistics 2026

133 cataloged theory courses, 662 units, 383 credits and 5231 theory hours across 14 SPPU 2024-pattern year-branch catalogs, computed from the same syllabus data that powers the subject pages. A course taught in several branches counts once per branch catalog. Data date 2026-11-05.

## Key findings

1.

PrepTracker catalogs the official SPPU 2024-pattern syllabus for 14 year-branch catalogs: 9 Second Year and 5 Third Year. One more branch (SE Automobile) is published by SPPU only as a draft and is marked as such.

[Link to this finding](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/research/sppu-syllabus-statistics-2026/#f-coverage)
2.

Across those catalogs, the library holds 133 cataloged theory-course entries, 662 units and 383 credits of theory, copied from the official SPPU syllabus PDFs. A course taught in more than one branch counts once per branch catalog.

[Link to this finding](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/research/sppu-syllabus-statistics-2026/#f-courses)
3.

The most common course size is 5 units: 130 of 133 theory courses (98%, rounded) have exactly 5 units.

[Link to this finding](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/research/sppu-syllabus-statistics-2026/#f-units)
4.

The largest catalog is TE Computer Engineering with 17 theory courses and 85 units; the smallest is SE Cyber Security with 7 courses and 35 units.

[Link to this finding](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/research/sppu-syllabus-statistics-2026/#f-branch-size)
5.

The First Year section covers 10 subjects with 50 units and 240 named topics, 34 credits in total, from the SPPU FE 2024-pattern syllabus.

[Link to this finding](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/research/sppu-syllabus-statistics-2026/#f-fe)
6.

Cataloged theory hours total 5231 across the final catalogs, summed from the per-unit hour allocations in the syllabi (semester hours, not weekly). Each branch page links the official SPPU PDF its numbers come from.

[Link to this finding](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/research/sppu-syllabus-statistics-2026/#f-hours)

## Methodology

- Source: the official SPPU syllabus PDFs, one linked at the bottom of every branch page. Counts are computed at build time from the catalog that renders those pages, so this page cannot drift from them.
- Included: theory courses on branches whose 2024-pattern syllabus SPPU has published as final, and the ten First Year subjects.
- Counting rule: courses are cataloged per branch and year, so a course taught in several branch catalogs counts once per catalog (133 entries, fewer unique titles). Hours are semester hours summed from each unit's hour allocation in the syllabus, not weekly hours.
- Excluded: SE Automobile (SPPU publishes it as a draft; its page is labeled draft), practical, lab and project courses, and the 2019-pattern TE pages kept for reference.
- Percentages are rounded to whole numbers; counts are exact.
- The data date is when the catalog last changed, not when the page was rebuilt.

## Cite this page

PrepTracker (2026). SPPU syllabus statistics 2026: 133 cataloged theory courses analyzed. https://preptracker.manavdev.site/research/sppu-syllabus-statistics-2026/ (data as of 2026-11-05).

## FAQ

**How many SPPU branches does PrepTracker cover?**

14 year-branch catalogs with final SPPU 2024-pattern syllabi: 9 Second Year and 5 Third Year. SE Automobile is published by SPPU as a draft and is labeled draft on its page.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/research/sppu-syllabus-statistics-2026/#faq-1)

**How many courses and units are cataloged?**

133 cataloged theory-course entries and 662 units across those catalogs, plus 10 First Year subjects with 50 units. A course taught in several branches counts once per branch catalog; practical, lab and project courses are not counted.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/research/sppu-syllabus-statistics-2026/#faq-2)

**Where do these numbers come from?**

Every count is computed at build time from the same syllabus data that renders the subject pages, and that data is copied from the official SPPU syllabus PDF linked at the bottom of each branch page. Nothing is estimated.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/research/sppu-syllabus-statistics-2026/#faq-3)

**How often do these numbers change?**

When SPPU publishes a new or revised syllabus and the catalog is updated. The date on this page is the data date, not a page rebuild date.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/research/sppu-syllabus-statistics-2026/#faq-4)

# First Year Engineering scheme, credits and marks

SPPU First Year Engineering, 2024 pattern (NEP 2020 compliant, Level 4.5). Both semesters carry 22 credits. This page copies the structure table from the official syllabus book and adds nothing to it.

22 credits per semester Theory: CCE 40 + End-Sem 60 Term work 25 per course

BSC-151-BESEngineering Mathematics-IIHrs Th/Tut/Pr 3 / 1 / -CCE 40 + End-Sem 60Term work 254 credits (3 / 1 / -)BSC-103-BES / BSC-102-BESEngineering Chemistry / Engineering PhysicsHrs Th/Tut/Pr 3 / - / 2CCE 40 + End-Sem 60Term work 254 credits (3 / - / 1)ESC-102-ELE / ESC-101-ETCBasic Electrical Engineering / Basic Electronics EngineeringHrs Th/Tut/Pr 2 / - / 2CCE 40 + End-Sem 60Term work 253 credits (2 / - / 1)ESC-104-CVL / ESC-103-MECEngineering Mechanics / Engineering GraphicsHrs Th/Tut/Pr 2 / - / 2CCE 40 + End-Sem 60Term work 253 credits (2 / - / 1)PCC-151-ITTProgramming and Problem SolvingHrs Th/Tut/Pr 2 / - / 2CCE 40 + End-Sem 60Term work 253 credits (2 / - / 1)VSE-102 / VSE-101Design Thinking and Idea Lab / Manufacturing Practice WorkshopHrs Th/Tut/Pr - / - / 2Term work 251 credits (- / - / 1)IKS-151Indian Knowledge SystemHrs Th/Tut/Pr - / 2 / -Term work 252 credits (- / 2 / -)CCC-151Co-Curricular Course-IIHrs Th/Tut/Pr - / - / 4Term work 252 credits (- / - / 2)Semester total12 + 3 + 14 hrs/weekCCE 200End-Sem 300Term work 20022 credits

Hrs are hours per week (Th theory, Tut tutorial, Pr practical). Where the book lists two courses with a slash, the pair is split across the two semesters, and the order flips in Semester II. CCE is Comprehensive Continuous Evaluation. The book leaves the oral and practical exam columns empty for every course. Marks follow the revised FE book issued in 2025, with effect from academic year 2025-26; the original July 2024 book had CCE 30 and End-Sem 70.

## FAQ

**How many credits does First Year Engineering have in the SPPU 2024 pattern?**

Each semester carries 22 credits: 12 theory, 3 tutorial and 7 practical or term-work credits. The SPPU credit framework handbook also sets a minimum of 22 credits per semester.

**Which subjects are in Semester I and Semester II?**

Engineering Mathematics-I is in Semester I and Engineering Mathematics-II in Semester II. Fundamentals of Programming Languages is in Semester I and Programming and Problem Solving in Semester II. The book pairs Physics with Chemistry, Electronics with Electrical, and Graphics with Mechanics, with one half of each pair in each semester. The full lists are in the tables above.

**How many marks is each course?**

A theory course is CCE 40 plus End-Sem 60, with 25 marks of term work on top. Courses without theory (workshop or lab, communication skills, co-curricular, Indian Knowledge System) carry 25 term-work marks only.

# SPPU grading system: grades, SGPA and CGPA

How marks become grades, grades become grade points, and grade points become SGPA. All numbers come from the SPPU credit framework handbook for the Faculty of Science and Technology.

## Grades and grade points

| Grade | Grade points | Marks (out of 100) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| O (Outstanding) | 10 | 90 to 100 |
| A+ (Excellent) | 9 | 75 to 89 |
| A (Very Good) | 8 | 60 to 74 |
| B+ (Good) | 7 | 55 to 59 |
| B (Above average) | 6 | 50 to 54 |
| C (Average) | 5 | 45 to 49 |
| D (Pass) | 4 | 40 to 44 |
| F (Fail) | 0 | Below the pass mark |
| Ab (Absent) | 0 | - |

The handbook prints the fail row as "Marks of 40 or less", which overlaps the D band (40 to 44). We show it as "below the pass mark" instead of guessing a cutoff. The handbook also labels two bands "B" (B+ for 55 to 59, B for 50 to 54). Check your university exam rules for the exact fail boundary.

## SGPA

SGPA is the credit-weighted average of grade points over every graded course in the semester:

SGPA = sum(grade points x credits) / total credits

Each graded row counts with its own credits, theory and term work or practical alike, the way the handbook lists them.

### Worked example (made-up numbers)

| Row | Credits | Grade | Points | Credits x points |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Theory A | 3 | A+ | 9 | 27 |
| Tutorial A | 1 | A | 8 | 8 |
| Theory B | 2 | B+ | 7 | 14 |
| Practical B | 1 | O | 10 | 10 |
| Total | 7 |  |  | 59 |

SGPA = 59 / 7 = 8.43. This example is ours. The handbook's own sample table shows 98 credit points over 22 credits as an SGPA of 8.9, which does not add up, so we did not copy it.

To work out your own SGPA, put your rows through the same steps as the worked example above: credits times grade points for each course, summed, divided by total credits.

## CGPA and class of degree

CGPA is calculated the same way as SGPA, over all semesters of the programme. If you clear a failed course or improve a grade, the new grade replaces the old one in both SGPA and CGPA. The class awarded depends on CGPA:

| CGPA | Class |
| --- | --- |
| 9.50 or more | Outstanding (O) |
| 8.50 to below 9.50 | Excellent (A+) |
| 7.50 to below 8.50 | Very Good (A) |
| 6.25 to below 7.50 | Good (B+) |
| 5.25 to below 6.25 | Above Average (B) |
| 4.75 to below 5.25 | Average (C) |
| 4.00 to below 4.75 | Pass (D) |
| Below 4.00 | Fail (F) |

We do not give a CGPA to percentage conversion. The handbook has a formula table for it, but its worked values do not match its own example, so we left it out rather than publish a number that might be wrong. Use the formula your college or the university notice gives you.

## FAQ

**What is the grade point for each grade in SPPU?**

O is 10, A+ is 9, A is 8, B+ is 7, B is 6, C is 5, D is 4, and F or Ab is 0, per the SPPU credit framework handbook.

**How is SGPA calculated?**

Multiply the grade points of each course by its credits, add them up, and divide by the total credits of the semester.

**Is there a CGPA to percentage formula here?**

No. The handbook formulas conflict with its own worked example, so this page does not publish a conversion.

# CCE, End-Sem and term work: how the marks are earned

The revised First Year 2024 pattern syllabus book (effective 2025-26) has a guidelines section for examination scheme. This page restates it in plain words, with nothing added.

CCE 40 End-Sem 60 Term work 25

## CCE: 40 marks, run by your college

Comprehensive Continuous Evaluation covers all five units and is held at institute level.

| Part | Marks | Units |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit test | 12 | Units I and II |
| Assignments or case study | 12 | Units III and IV |
| Seminar presentation, open book test or quiz | 6 | Unit V |
| Mini project, project-based learning or group activity | 10 | Any unit |

The book's example timeline: Units I and II in weeks 1 to 4 with the unit test in week 5, Units III and IV in weeks 6 to 8 with assignments collected in week 9, Unit V in weeks 10 to 12 and the seminar, open book test or quiz in week 13. The unit test is built on Bloom's taxonomy levels. For the seminar, you give a talk on a Unit V topic and answer questions, with slides and a 2 to 3 page summary.

## End-Sem: 60 marks, set by the university

A written theory paper on all five units, scheduled by the university, with question papers delivered through QPD (Question Paper Delivery). It is designed on Bloom's taxonomy, from remembering up to creating.

The revised book allocates 12 marks per unit across the five units for the 60, with questions set on Bloom's taxonomy levels.

## Term work: 25 marks, from your journal

Term work is continuous assessment of the journal of practical assignments, with a reflection on each. The book's evaluation criteria:

| Criterion | Weight |
| --- | --- |
| Completeness | 20% |
| Quality of work | 40% |
| Organization | 20% |
| Presentation | 10% |
| Creativity and engagement | 10% |

The book's sample timeline has the journal finalized in week 10 and submitted in week 11. The final term-work grade goes to SPPU at the end of the semester.

See the [scheme and credits tables](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/first-year-scheme-credits/) for which courses carry which marks, and the [grading page](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/grading-system-sgpa/) for how they turn into grades.

## FAQ

**How is the 40 marks CCE divided in SPPU 2024 pattern?**

Unit test 12 marks on Units I and II, assignments or case study 12 marks on Units III and IV, a seminar, open book test or quiz for 6 marks on Unit V, and a mini project or group activity for 10 marks on any unit.

**Who conducts the End-Sem exam?**

The university. It is a 60 mark written paper on all five units, and the question paper is delivered through QPD.

**What decides the term work marks?**

Your journal of practical assignments, judged on completeness, quality, organization, presentation and creativity, as described in the syllabus book.

# Engineering Mathematics-I syllabus

SPPU First Year Engineering, 2024 pattern. Course code BSC-101-BES. Five units, 40 hours of theory, with the marks scheme, outcomes and books taken from the official syllabus book.

4 credits (3 theory + 1 tutorial) CCE 40 + End-Sem 60 Term work 25 5 units x 8 hours

40 hours of theory

05 . units

04 . credits

## At a glance

Course codeBSC-101-BES

LevelFirst Year Engineering, SPPU 2024 pattern

Units5

Named topics27

Theory hours40

Credits4 (3 theory + 1 tutorial)

## Unit-wise syllabus

UNIT I

### Single Variable Calculus

8 hours

Rolle’s Theorem Mean Value Theorems Taylor's and Maclaurin's Series Indeterminate Forms L' Hospital's Rule Fourier series (Full range & Half range) Harmonic analysis

UNIT II

### Multivariable Calculus – Partial Differentiation

8 hours

Limits & Continuity of several variables Partial Derivatives Euler's Theorem on Homogeneous functions Partial derivative of Composite Function Total Derivative Change of Independent variables

UNIT III

### Applications of Partial Differentiation

8 hours

Jacobian and its applications Errors and Approximations Maxima and Minima of functions of two variables Lagrange's method of undetermined multipliers

UNIT IV

### Matrices and System of Linear Equations

8 hours

Rank of a Matrix System of Linear Equations Linear Dependence and Independence Linear and Orthogonal Transformations Applications in Engineering

UNIT V

### Eigen Values, Eigen Vectors and Diagonalization

8 hours

Eigen Values and Eigen Vectors Cayley Hamilton theorem Diagonalization of a matrix Reduction of Quadratic forms to Canonical form Applications in Engineering

## Marks and credits

| Head | Marks | Credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theory: CCE | 40 | 3 |
| Theory: End-Semester | 60 | 3 |
| Tutorial / term work | 25 | 1 |

The prerequisites listed in the syllabus are differentiation, integration, maxima and minima, matrices and determinants. The course aims to build the calculus, Fourier series and linear algebra needed in later engineering subjects.

## Course outcomes

1. CO1 Apply mean value theorems and their generalizations leading to Taylor and Maclaurin series. Determine the Fourier series representation and harmonic analysis of periodic functions. Covers Unit I
2. CO2 Evaluate derivative functions of several variables. Covers Unit II
3. CO3 Apply the Jacobian to find partial derivatives of implicit functions and functional dependence. Use partial derivatives for errors, approximations and extreme values. Covers Unit III
4. CO4 Use matrices and linear algebra to analyse systems of linear equations, linear dependence and independence, and linear and orthogonal transformations. Covers Unit IV
5. CO5 Determine eigen values and eigen vectors, diagonalize a matrix and reduce a quadratic form to canonical form. Covers Unit V

## Books

### Text books

- Higher Engineering Mathematics by B. V. Ramana (Tata McGraw Hill)
- Higher Engineering Mathematics by B. S. Grewal (Khanna Publication)

### Reference books

- Advanced Engineering Mathematics by Erwin Kreyszig (Wiley Eastern Ltd.)
- Advanced Engineering Mathematics by M. D. Greenberg (Pearson Education)
- Advanced Engineering Mathematics by Peter V. O’Neil (Thomson Learning)
- Thomas’ Calculus by George B. Thomas (Addison-Wesley, Pearson)
- Applied Mathematics (Vol. I & II) by P. N. Wartikar and J. N. Wartikar (Vidyarthi Griha Prakashan, Pune)
- Elementary Linear Algebra by Ron Larson and David C. Falvo (Houghton Mifflin Harcourt)

## Video lectures

The syllabus lists one NPTEL / YouTube playlist for this course: [Engineering Mathematics-I playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLbRMhDVUMngeVrxtbBz-n8HvP8KAWBpI5).

# Engineering Physics syllabus

SPPU First Year Engineering, 2024 pattern. Course code BSC-102-BES. Five units, 40 hours of theory and a practical component, with the marks scheme, outcomes and books taken from the official syllabus book.

4 credits (3 theory + 1 practical) CCE 40 + End-Sem 60 Term work 25 5 units x 8 hours

40 hours of theory

05 . units

04 . credits

## At a glance

Course codeBSC-102-BES

LevelFirst Year Engineering, SPPU 2024 pattern

Units5

Named topics28

Theory hours40

Credits4 (3 theory + 1 tutorial)

## Unit-wise syllabus

UNIT I

### Fundamentals of Photonics

8 hours

Laser: Spontaneous/Stimulated emission CO2 laser construction & working Holography: Recording & Reconstruction Optical fibers: NA, Attenuation Fiber optic communication advantages

UNIT II

### Quantum Physics

8 hours

de Broglie hypothesis & Matter waves Schrödinger's time dependent/independent equations Particle in a rigid box Quantum tunneling & STM Quantum computing: Qbits, Superposition, Entanglement

UNIT III

### Wave Optics

8 hours

Interference in thin films (Reflected system) Newton's rings Polarization (PPL, CPL, EPL) Malu's law Double refraction (Huygens theory) LCDs & 3D Movies

UNIT IV

### Semiconductor Physics and Ultrasonics

8 hours

Fermi level & Fermi energy PN junction diode (Fermi level basis) Solar cell: IV characteristics & Fill factor Hall effect Ultrasonics: Piezoelectric generation Flaw detection & Thickness measurement

UNIT V

### Nanoparticles and Superconductivity

8 hours

Quantum confinement Synthesis: Ball milling, PVD GMR effect & HDD Superconductivity (Type I & II) Meissner effect & BCS theory SQUID & Maglev train

## Marks and credits

| Head | Marks | Credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theory: CCE | 40 | 3 |
| Theory: End-Semester | 60 | 3 |
| Practical / term work | 25 | 1 |

The prerequisites listed in the syllabus are Bohr’s atomic theory, properties of mechanical and electromagnetic waves, Huygens’ principle and wavefront, interference and polarization of light, wave particle duality, intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors, basics of magnetism, trigonometry and calculus. The course aims to teach the fundamentals of physics through hands-on experiments and extend them to engineering applications. The practical side is 2 hours a week, and any 8 experiments from a list of 12 are performed.

## Course outcomes

1. CO1 Develop the understanding of the working principle of lasers and optical fibers and extend it to holography and fiber optic communication.
2. CO2 Deduce Schrödinger’s wave equations and apply them to problems on bound states, using the fundamentals of quantum physics.
3. CO3 Explain interference in thin films, polarization and double refraction, and connect them to the anti-reflection coating and LCD.
4. CO4 Understand Fermi level and Fermi energy in semiconductors from Fermi Dirac statistics and relate them to semiconductor devices. Extend ultrasonics to thickness measurement and flaw detection.
5. CO5 Explain the properties of nanoparticles and their engineering applications. Explain superconductivity and its engineering applications.

## Books

### Text books

- A Textbook of Engineering Physics by M. N. Avadhanulu, P. G. Kshirsagar and TVS Arun Murthy (S. Chand Publications)
- Engineering Physics by R. K. Gaur and S. L. Gupta (Dhanpat Rai Publications)

### Reference books

- Optics by Ajoy Ghatak (Tata McGraw Hill)
- Introduction to Solid State Physics by C. Kittel (Wiley and Sons)
- Quantum Mechanics by A. K. Ghatak and S. Lokanathan (Laxmi Publications)
- Nanotechnology: Principles and Practices by Dr. S. K. Kulkarni (Capital Publishing)
- Physics for Scientists and Engineers with Modern Physics by Serway and Jewett (Cengage Publications)

## Video lectures

The syllabus lists two video resources, plus the Feynman Lectures and Beiser’s Concepts of Modern Physics as e-books: [Lectures by Walter Lewin](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCiEHVhv0SBMpP75JbzJShqw), [Quantum Mechanics lecture series by Prof. H. C. Verma](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLWweJWdB_GuISnGkAafMpzzDBvTHg02At).

# Engineering Chemistry syllabus

SPPU First Year Engineering, 2024 pattern. Course code BSC-103-BES. Five units, 40 hours of theory and a practical component, with the marks scheme, outcomes and books taken from the official syllabus book.

4 credits (3 theory + 1 practical) CCE 40 + End-Sem 60 Term work 25 5 units x 8 hours

40 hours of theory

05 . units

04 . credits

## At a glance

Course codeBSC-103-BES

LevelFirst Year Engineering, SPPU 2024 pattern

Units5

Named topics24

Theory hours40

Credits4 (3 theory + 1 tutorial)

## Unit-wise syllabus

UNIT I

### Water Technology

8 hours

Impurities & Hardness (EDTA method) Alkalinity determination Boiler troubles: Priming, Foaming, Scale, Sludge Zeolite & Demineralization methods Reverse Osmosis & Electrodialysis

UNIT II

### Instrumental Methods of Analysis

8 hours

Conductometry (Acid-Base Titrations) pHmetry (Strong Acid-Strong Base) UV-Visible Spectroscopy Beer's law & Lambert's law Instrumentation (Double beam)

UNIT III

### Advanced Engineering Materials

8 hours

Polymers: Thermoplastics vs Thermosetting Specialty Polymers: Polycarbonate, PHBV Conducting Polymers (Polyacetylene) Nanomaterials: Graphene, CNTs, Quantum dots

UNIT IV

### Energy Sources

8 hours

Calorific value (Bomb & Boy’s calorimeter) Coal Analysis (Proximate & Ultimate) Biodiesel & Power alcohol Hydrogen fuel cells Lithium Ion Battery

UNIT V

### Corrosion and its Prevention

8 hours

Dry & Wet corrosion mechanisms Pilling-Bedworth's rule Cathodic Protection (Sacrificial/Impressed current) Electroplating & Hot dipping Anti-corrosive paints

## Marks and credits

| Head | Marks | Credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theory: CCE | 40 | 3 |
| Theory: End-Semester | 60 | 3 |
| Practical / term work | 25 | 1 |

The prerequisites listed in the syllabus are types of titrations, structure property relationship, classification and properties of polymers, electromagnetic radiation and the electrochemical series. The course covers water quality analysis, electro-analytical techniques, specialty polymers and nanomaterials, fuels, and corrosion. The practical side is 2 hours a week, and any 8 experiments from a list of 11 are performed.

## Course outcomes

1. CO1 Understand the practical approaches and techniques needed to monitor water quality. Covers Unit I
2. CO2 Select appropriate electro-analytical techniques for understanding materials. Covers Unit II
3. CO3 Demonstrate the structure and properties of advanced engineering materials for technological applications. Covers Unit III
4. CO4 Analyse different types of conventional and alternative fuels. Covers Unit IV
5. CO5 Explain the causes of corrosion and the methods for minimizing it. Covers Unit V

## Books

### Text books

- Textbook of Engineering Chemistry by Dr. S. S. Dara and Dr. S. S. Umare (S. Chand & Company Ltd.)
- Engineering Chemistry by O. G. Palanna (Tata McGraw Hill Education Pvt. Ltd.)
- Textbook of Engineering Chemistry by Dr. Sunita Rattan (S. K. Kataria & Sons)

### Reference books

- Basic Concept of Analytical Chemistry, 2nd ed., by S. M. Khopkar (New Age International)
- Instrumental Methods of Chemical Analysis by G. R. Chatwal and S. K. Anand (Himalaya Publishing House)
- Spectroscopy of Organic Compounds, 2nd ed., by P. S. Kalsi (New Age International)
- Polymer Science by V. R. Gowarikar, N. V. Viswanathan and Jayadev Sreedhar (Wiley Eastern Limited)
- Inorganic Chemistry, 5th ed., by Shriver and Atkins (Oxford University Press)
- Fundamentals of Nanotechnology by G. L. Hornyak, J. J. Moore, H. F. Tibbals and J. Dutta (CRC Press)

Any 8 from the list of 11 in the syllabus. They include hardness by EDTA, alkalinity, pH and conductometric titrations, proximate analysis of coal and preparing biodiesel.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-chemistry/#faq-4)

**Which books does the syllabus list?**

Three text books (Dara and Umare, Palanna, Rattan) and six reference books, including Khopkar, Chatwal and Anand, Kalsi and Shriver and Atkins.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-chemistry/#faq-5)

**Is there an official video course?**

The syllabus lists one NPTEL course, number 113104082. It is linked on this page.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-chemistry/#faq-6)

# Basic Electronics Engineering syllabus

SPPU First Year Engineering, 2024 pattern. Course code ESC-101-ETC. Five units, 30 hours of theory and a practical component, with the marks scheme, outcomes and books taken from the official syllabus book.

3 credits (2 theory + 1 practical) CCE 40 + End-Sem 60 Term work 25 5 units x 6 hours

30 hours of theory

05 . units

03 . credits

## At a glance

Course codeESC-101-ETC

LevelFirst Year Engineering, SPPU 2024 pattern

Units5

Named topics23

Theory hours30

Credits3 (2 theory + 1 tutorial)

## Unit-wise syllabus

UNIT I

### Diodes and Applications

6 hours

PN Junction Diode Characteristics Rectifiers (Half, Full Wave, Bridge) Capacitor filter LED & Photodiode Diode as a switch

UNIT II

### Transistors and Technology

6 hours

BJT: CE Configuration & Amplifier EMOSFET: Switch & Amplifier VLSI Technology Introduction CMOS Manufacturing (N-Well)

UNIT III

### Logic Gates and Digital Circuits

6 hours

Number Systems (Binary, Hex, Octal) Logic Gates (Universal Gates) Half & Full Adders Flip Flops (SR, JK, T, D) Microprocessor vs Microcontroller

UNIT IV

### Op-Amp and Electronic Instruments

6 hours

Op-Amp Block Diagram Inverting & Non-inverting Amplifier Digital Multimeter Function Generator Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO)

UNIT V

### Sensors and Communication Systems

6 hours

Sensors: LVDT, Thermocouple, RTD, Strain Gauge IoT Data Acquisition System GSM System Block Diagram Wired vs Wireless Media

## Marks and credits

| Head | Marks | Credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theory: CCE | 40 | 2 |
| Theory: End-Semester | 60 | 2 |
| Practical / term work | 25 | 1 |

The prerequisites listed in the syllabus are basic physics and mathematics, semiconductor physics, digital electronics, circuit theory, analog electronics, and sensors and transducers. The course covers diodes, transistors, digital circuits, op-amps with instruments, and sensors with communication systems. The practical side is 2 hours a week, and any 8 experiments from a list of 10 are performed.

## Course outcomes

1. CO1 Know the working of the P-N junction diode and its use as a rectifier and switch, plus the basics of the LED and photodiode. Covers Unit I
2. CO2 Understand the working of the BJT and MOSFET, their characteristics, and compare them. Covers Unit II
3. CO3 Learn logic gates and how digital circuits are realized. Covers Unit III
4. CO4 Understand how an op-amp and the common electronic instruments work. Covers Unit IV
5. CO5 Select sensors by working principle for specific applications and connect them to a communication system. Covers Unit V

## Books

### Text books

- Electronic Devices by Thomas L. Floyd, 9th edition (Pearson)
- Modern Digital Electronics by R. P. Jain, 4th edition (Tata McGraw Hill)
- Electronic Instrumentation by H. S. Kalsi, 3rd edition (Tata McGraw Hill)
- Sensors and Transducers by D. Patranabis, 2nd edition (PHI)
- Electronic Communication Systems by Kennedy and Davis, 4th edition (Tata McGraw Hill)
- Mobile Wireless Communication by M. Schwartz (Cambridge University Press)

### Reference books

- Digital Fundamentals by Thomas L. Floyd, 11th edition (Pearson)
- Mobile Communication by J. Schiller, 2nd edition (Pearson)
- Sensors Handbook by S. Soloman, 2nd edition
- CMOS Circuit Design, Layout and Simulation by Baker, 2nd edition (Wiley IEEE Press)

## Video lectures

The syllabus lists three NPTEL courses for this subject: [NPTEL course 117103063](https://nptel.ac.in/courses/117103063), [NPTEL course 117103064](https://nptel.ac.in/courses/117103064), [NPTEL course 106105166](https://archive.nptel.ac.in/courses/106/105/106105166/).

# Basic Electrical Engineering syllabus

SPPU First Year Engineering, 2024 pattern. Course code ESE-102-ELE. Five units, 30 hours of theory and a practical component, with the marks scheme, outcomes and books taken from the official syllabus book.

3 credits (2 theory + 1 practical) CCE 40 + End-Sem 60 Term work 25 5 units x 6 hours

30 hours of theory

05 . units

03 . credits

## At a glance

Course codeESC-102-ELE

LevelFirst Year Engineering, SPPU 2024 pattern

Units5

Named topics26

Theory hours30

Credits3 (2 theory + 1 tutorial)

## Unit-wise syllabus

UNIT I

### Elementary Concepts and DC Circuits

6 hours

Resistance, EMF, Potential Difference Overview of Power System (Generation, Transmission, Distribution) Kirchhoff’s Laws (KVL/KCL) & Loop Analysis Star-Delta Transformation Superposition Theorem

UNIT II

### Electromagnetism

6 hours

Magnetic Circuits (Flux, MMF, Reluctance) Series Magnetic Circuits Faraday's Laws of Electromagnetic Induction Fleming's Right-hand Rule Statically & Dynamically Induced EMF Self & Mutual Inductance Energy stored in Magnetic Field

UNIT III

### AC Fundamentals

6 hours

Generation of Sinusoidal Voltages RMS, Average, Peak, Form Factor Phasor Representation (Rectangular/Polar) Phase Difference (Lagging/Leading) Pure R, L, C Circuits

UNIT IV

### AC Circuits

6 hours

Series R-L, R-C, R-L-C Circuits Impedance, Power Factor, Phasor Diagrams Active, Reactive, Apparent Power Resonance in RLC Series Three Phase AC (Star & Delta Relations)

UNIT V

### Introduction to Electric Machines

6 hours

Single Phase Transformer (Principle, EMF Eq, Efficiency) DC Motors (Construction, Types, Characteristics) Three Phase Induction Motor (RMF principle) Single Phase Induction Motor (Split Phase, Capacitor Types)

## Marks and credits

| Head | Marks | Credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theory: CCE | 40 | 2 |
| Theory: End-Semester | 60 | 2 |
| Practical / term work | 25 | 1 |

The prerequisites listed in the syllabus are electric charges and fields, Coulomb’s laws, voltage, potential, current, Ohm’s law, magnetism, EMF, Faraday’s laws, alternating current, the AC generator and power. The course covers AC and DC circuit analysis, the working of basic electric machines, wiring components and schemes, and the electricity bill. The practical side is 2 hours a week, and any 8 experiments from a list of 10 are performed.

## Course outcomes

1. CO1 Apply Kirchhoff’s laws, the superposition theorem and network simplification to DC circuit analysis. Covers Unit I
2. CO2 Analyse magnetic circuit parameters, self and mutual inductance, and electromotive forces. Covers Unit II
3. CO3 Calculate AC quantities using equations, waveforms and phasor diagrams. Covers Unit III
4. CO4 Compute the voltage, current and power of 1-phase and 3-phase AC circuits. Covers Unit IV
5. CO5 Understand the working principle of the 1-phase transformer and of DC and induction motors, and their practical uses. Covers Unit V

## Books

### Text books

- ABC of Electrical Engineering by B. L. Theraja and A. K. Theraja (S. Chand Publications, 2012)
- Basic Electrical Engineering by D. C. Kulshreshtha, 2nd edition, 2019 (McGraw Hill Education)

### Reference books

- Basic Electrical Engineering by C. L. Wadhwa, 5th edition, 2024 (New Age International)
- Electrical Machines by S. K. Bhattacharya, 2nd edition, 2008 (McGraw Hill Education)
- Basic Electrical Engineering by T. K. Nagsarkar and M. S. Sukhija, 2nd edition, 2018 (Oxford University Press)

## Video lectures

The syllabus lists one NPTEL course for this subject: [NPTEL course 108105112](https://nptel.ac.in/courses/108105112).

[Open Basic Electrical Engineering in the app](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/#/subject/elec)

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/basic-electrical-engineering/#faq-2)

**How many units are there?**

Five units of 6 hours each, 30 hours in total: elementary concepts and DC circuits, electromagnetism, AC fundamentals, AC circuits, and an introduction to electric machines.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/basic-electrical-engineering/#faq-3)

**How many experiments do I have to do?**

Any 8 from the list of 10 in the syllabus. They include verifying Kirchhoff’s laws and the superposition theorem, a transformer loading test, RLC resonance, three-phase star and delta relations, and reading a single-phase LT electricity bill.

# Engineering Mechanics syllabus

SPPU First Year Engineering, 2024 pattern. Course code ESC-104-CVL. Five units, 30 hours of theory and a practical component, with the marks scheme, outcomes and books taken from the official syllabus book.

3 credits (2 theory + 1 practical) CCE 40 + End-Sem 60 Term work 25 5 units x 6 hours

30 hours of theory

05 . units

03 . credits

## At a glance

Course codeESC-104-CVL

LevelFirst Year Engineering, SPPU 2024 pattern

Units5

Named topics21

Theory hours30

Credits3 (2 theory + 1 tutorial)

## Unit-wise syllabus

UNIT I

### Force systems and its resultants

6 hours

Resolution & Composition of forces Varignon's theorem Distributed Forces Centroid of composite figures Moment of Inertia (Parallel/Perpendicular axis)

UNIT II

### Equilibrium

6 hours

Free body diagram Three Force Principle (Lami’s) Equilibrium of Concurrent/Parallel/General forces Types of beams, loads & supports

UNIT III

### Friction and trusses

6 hours

Laws of Coulomb friction Angle of repose & Cone of friction Ladder & Belt friction Simple Trusses: Method of Joints & Sections

UNIT IV

### Kinematics of particle

6 hours

Rectilinear motion (Variable acceleration) Curvilinear motion Projectile motion Normal & Tangential components

UNIT V

### Kinetics of particle

6 hours

Newton's Second Law Work Energy Principle Impulse Momentum Principle Coefficient of Restitution & Impact

## Marks and credits

| Head | Marks | Credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theory: CCE | 40 | 2 |
| Theory: End-Semester | 60 | 2 |
| Practical / term work | 25 | 1 |

The prerequisites listed in the syllabus are basic calculus, trigonometry, geometrical expressions, laws of motion, the concept of mass and acceleration, with a base in engineering mathematics and physics. The course teaches the basics of mechanics and applies them to forces, loads and moments. The practical side is 2 hours a week: four compulsory experiments, four graphical solutions and an assignment of at least four examples per unit.

## Course outcomes

1. CO1 Understand forces, moments and couples in a two-dimensional force system. Covers Unit I
2. CO2 Apply the free body diagram to static equilibrium in a two-dimensional force system. Covers Unit II
3. CO3 Analyse practical examples involving friction and two force members. Covers Unit III
4. CO4 Analyse rectilinear and curvilinear motion of a particle. Covers Unit IV
5. CO5 Apply Newton’s second law, the work energy principle and the impulse momentum principle to particles. Covers Unit V

## Books

### Text books

- Engineering Mechanics by Ferdinand Singer, 3rd edition (Harper and Row)
- Engineering Mechanics (Statics and Dynamics) by R. C. Hibbeler (Pearson Education)

### Reference books

- Engineering Mechanics by S. Timoshenko and Young (Tata McGraw Hill Education Pvt. Ltd., New Delhi)
- Vector Mechanics for Engineers: Statics by Beer and Johnston (Tata McGraw Hill)
- Vector Mechanics for Engineers: Dynamics by Beer and Johnston (Tata McGraw Hill)
- Engineering Mechanics: Statics and Dynamics by J. L. Meriam and L. G. Kraige (John Wiley and Sons)

## Video lectures

The syllabus lists no NPTEL or video resources for this subject.

## Track it in PrepTracker

Tick off each unit as you finish it, and keep your own notes and links in one place. It is free and needs no account.

[Open Engineering Mechanics in the app](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/#/subject/mech)

## FAQ

**How many credits is Engineering Mechanics in the SPPU 2024 pattern?**

ESC-104-CVL carries 3 credits: 2 for theory (2 hours a week) and 1 for practical (2 hours a week).

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-mechanics/#faq-1)

**How are the marks split?**

Theory is graded out of 100: CCE (continuous internal evaluation) 40 and End-Semester 60. Term work is a separate 25 marks tied to the practical credit.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-mechanics/#faq-2)

**How many units are there?**

Five units of 6 hours each, 30 hours in total: force systems and resultants, equilibrium, friction and trusses, kinematics of a particle, and kinetics of a particle.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-mechanics/#faq-3)

**What does the lab journal contain?**

Four compulsory experiments (polygon law of forces, support reaction of a beam, coefficient of friction, coefficient of restitution), four graphical solutions (concurrent and parallel equilibrium, truss member forces, moment of inertia) and an assignment of at least four examples on each unit.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-mechanics/#faq-4)

**Which books does the syllabus list?**

Two text books (Singer, and Hibbeler) and four reference books, including Timoshenko and Young, Beer and Johnston (statics and dynamics) and Meriam and Kraige.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-mechanics/#faq-5)

# Fundamentals of Programming Languages syllabus

SPPU First Year Engineering, 2024 pattern. Course code ESC-105-COM. Five units of C programming, 30 hours of theory and a practical component, with the marks scheme, outcomes and books taken from the official syllabus book.

3 credits (2 theory + 1 practical) CCE 40 + End-Sem 60 Term work 25 5 units x 6 hours

30 hours of theory

05 . units

03 . credits

## At a glance

Course codeESC-105-COM

LevelFirst Year Engineering, SPPU 2024 pattern

Units5

Named topics24

Theory hours30

Credits3 (2 theory + 1 tutorial)

## Unit-wise syllabus

UNIT I

### Intro to Program Planning & C Programming

6 hours

Algorithms & Flowcharts C Tokens, Keywords, Identifiers Constants, Variables, Data types Storage Classes Program compilation Process

UNIT II

### Operators and Expressions

6 hours

Arithmetic, Relational, Logical Operators Increment/Decrement Operators Bitwise Operators Operator Precedence Type casting

UNIT III

### Control Flow

6 hours

If-Else, Switch Statement Loops: While, Do-While, For Break and Continue Goto Statement

UNIT IV

### Arrays

6 hours

One Dimensional Arrays Two-dimensional Arrays Character Arrays and Strings String handling Functions Matrix multiplication

UNIT V

### User Defined Functions

6 hours

Function definition & declaration Call by value/reference Recursion Structures (Declaration, Initialization) Tower of Hanoi

## Marks and credits

| Head | Marks | Credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theory: CCE | 40 | 2 |
| Theory: End-Semester | 60 | 2 |
| Practical / term work | 25 | 1 |

The prerequisites listed in the syllabus are basics of computers and basic mathematics. The course teaches C programming: algorithms, operators, control flow, arrays and strings, and user defined functions with structures. The practical side is 2 hours a week: any 6 to 8 programming assignments from a list of 10, and the syllabus also suggests four mini-projects such as a calculator, a dice roller and a number guessing game.

## Course outcomes

1. CO1 Design algorithms for simple computational problems. Covers Unit I
2. CO2 Use mathematical and logical operators and expressions. Covers Unit II
3. CO3 Apply control flow structures for decision making. Covers Unit III
4. CO4 Design a solution using arrays, character arrays and strings. Covers Unit IV
5. CO5 Design and apply user defined functions and structures. Covers Unit V

## Books

### Text books

- Programming in ANSI C, 8th edition, by E. Balagurusamy

### Reference books

- Programming with C (Schaum’s Outline Series), 2nd edition, by B. S. Gottfried (McGraw-Hill, 1996)
- Programming in C, 3rd edition, by S. C. Kochan (Sams Publishing, 2004)
- The C Programming Language, 2nd edition, by B. W. Kernighan and D. M. Ritchie (Prentice Hall, 1988)
- The Practice of Programming by B. W. Kernighan and R. Pike (Addison-Wesley, 1999)
- C: How to Program, 8th edition, by H. M. Deitel and P. J. Deitel (Pearson Education, 2015)
- C in a Nutshell: The Definitive Reference, 2nd edition, by P. Prinz and T. Crawford (O’Reilly Media, 2016)

## Video lectures

The syllabus lists two NPTEL courses for this subject: [NPTEL course noc22_cs40](https://onlinecourses.nptel.ac.in/noc22_cs40/preview), [NPTEL course noc23_cs53](https://onlinecourses.nptel.ac.in/noc23_cs53/preview).

C. The five units cover program planning and the basics of C, operators and expressions, control flow, arrays and strings, and user defined functions with structures.

Any 6 to 8 from the list of 10 in the syllabus. They include prime and factorial programs, a Fibonacci series, array operations, string operations and a structure for employee details. Instructors may also assign a mini-project.

# Engineering Graphics syllabus

SPPU First Year Engineering, 2024 pattern. Course code ESC-103-MEC. Five units, 30 hours of theory and a drawing practical, with the marks scheme, outcomes and books taken from the official syllabus book.

3 credits (2 theory + 1 practical) CCE 40 + End-Sem 60 Term work 25 5 units x 6 hours

30 hours of theory

05 . units

03 . credits

## At a glance

Course codeESC-103-MEC

LevelFirst Year Engineering, SPPU 2024 pattern

Units5

Named topics19

Theory hours30

Credits3 (2 theory + 1 tutorial)

## Unit-wise syllabus

UNIT I

### Fundamentals & Projection of Point/Line

6 hours

Drawing instruments & Sheet layout Dimensioning rules Projection of Points Projection of Lines (Inclined to both planes) Traces of Lines

UNIT II

### Projection of Plane

6 hours

Planes parallel/perpendicular to reference Planes inclined to one plane Planes inclined to both reference planes

UNIT III

### Engineering Curves and Development

6 hours

Conic Sections (Ellipse, Parabola, Hyperbola) Helix, Cycloid, Involute, Archimedean Spiral Development of Lateral Surfaces (Prism, Pyramid, Cylinder, Cone)

UNIT IV

### Orthographic Projection

6 hours

First & Third angle method Hidden features Conversion of 3D to 2D views Sectional Views

UNIT V

### Isometric Projection

6 hours

Isometric lines & planes Isometric scale Construction of Isometric views from Orthographic Isometric Projection vs Isometric View

## Marks and credits

| Head | Marks | Credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theory: CCE | 40 | 2 |
| Theory: End-Semester | 60 | 2 |
| Practical / term work | 25 | 1 |

The prerequisites listed in the syllabus are basic geometric shapes, basic linear and angular measurements and construction, the lines, circles and polygons of coordinate geometry, and computer literacy. The course builds the ability to draw physical objects for engineering communication and introduces drawing and design software. For the practical, the assignments are drawn on A2 sheets, and two problems must be drawn in a CAD software.

## Course outcomes

1. CO1 Explain the fundamentals of engineering graphics and geometric construction, and prepare drawings for points and lines using projections. Covers Unit I
2. CO2 Apply the types of projection methods to prepare drawings of planes. Covers Unit II
3. CO3 Construct engineering curves, show their applications, and draw the development of the lateral surface of a solid. Covers Unit III
4. CO4 Apply orthographic projection to draw several 2D views of an object. Covers Unit IV
5. CO5 Use visualization skill to draw an isometric projection from given orthographic views. Covers Unit V

## Books

### Text books

- Engineering Drawing by N. D. Bhatt and V. M. Panchal, 2016 (Charotar Publication, Anand)
- Engineering and Graphics by K. Venugopal, 2015 (New Age International, New Delhi)
- Engineering Drawing with Introduction to AutoCAD by D. A. Jolhe, 2015 (Tata McGraw Hill, New Delhi)
- A First Course in Engineering Drawing by K. Rathnam, 2018 (Springer Nature Singapore)

### Reference books

- Engineering Drawing and Design by D. P. Madsen and D. A. Madsen, 2016 (Delmar Publishers)
- Machine Drawing by N. D. Bhatt, 2018 (Charotar Publishing House, Anand)
- A Textbook of Engineering Drawing by R. K. Dhawan, 2000 (S. Chand, New Delhi)
- The Fundamentals of Engineering Drawing: With an Introduction to Interactive Computer Graphics for Design and Production by W. J. Luzadder and J. M. Duff, 1992 (Peachpit Press)
- Principles of Engineering Graphics by F. E. Giesecke and others, 1990 (Macmillan Publishing)

## Video lectures

The syllabus lists NPTEL resources, including: [NPTEL: Engineering Graphics and Design](https://onlinecourses.nptel.ac.in/noc21_me128/preview), [NPTEL: Introduction and Geometric Construction](https://archive.nptel.ac.in/content/storage2/courses/112103019/module1/lec3/1.html).

## Track it in PrepTracker

Tick off each unit as you finish it, and keep your own notes and links in one place. It is free and needs no account.

[Open Engineering Graphics in the app](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/#/subject/graph)

## FAQ

**How many credits is Engineering Graphics in the SPPU 2024 pattern?**

ESC-103-MEC carries 3 credits: 2 for theory (2 hours a week) and 1 for practical (2 hours a week).

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-graphics/#faq-1)

**How are the marks split?**

Theory is graded out of 100: CCE (continuous internal evaluation) 40 and End-Semester 60. Term work is a separate 25 marks tied to the practical credit.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-graphics/#faq-2)

**How many units are there?**

Five units of 6 hours each, 30 hours in total: fundamentals with projection of points and lines, projection of planes, engineering curves with development of surfaces, orthographic projection, and isometric projection.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-graphics/#faq-3)

**What are the drawing assignments?**

Five sets of two problems each: projection of lines, projection of planes, engineering curves with development of lateral surfaces, orthographic projections and isometric projections. They are drawn on A2 sheets, and two problems must be drawn using CAD software.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-graphics/#faq-4)

**Which angle of projection is used?**

The syllabus covers both first angle and third angle methods in orthographic projection. Typical problems are solved by the first angle method, and projection of lines is taught in first angle projection.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-graphics/#faq-5)

**Which books does the syllabus list?**

Four text books (Bhatt and Panchal, Venugopal, Jolhe, Rathnam) and five reference books, including Madsen and Madsen, Dhawan and Giesecke.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-graphics/#faq-6)

# Engineering Mathematics-II syllabus

SPPU First Year Engineering, 2024 pattern, Semester II. Course code BSC-151-BES. Five units, 40 hours of theory, with the marks scheme, outcomes and books taken from the official syllabus book.

4 credits (3 theory + 1 tutorial) CCE 40 + End-Sem 60 Term work 25 5 units x 8 hours

40 hours of theory

05 . units

04 . credits

## At a glance

Course codeBSC-151-BES

LevelFirst Year Engineering, SPPU 2024 pattern

Units5

Named topics31

Theory hours40

Credits4 (3 theory + 1 tutorial)

## Unit-wise syllabus

UNIT I

### First Order Ordinary Differential Equations

8 hours

Exact Differential Equations Equations reducible to exact equations Linear Differential Equations Equations reducible to Linear equations Applications: Orthogonal Trajectories Newton's Law of Cooling Electrical Circuits

UNIT II

### Linear Differential Equations with Constant Coefficients

8 hours

LDE with constant coefficients Homogeneous Linear Differential Equations Legendre's Linear Equations Applications: L-C-R Circuits

UNIT III

### Fourier Series

8 hours

Periodic functions Dirichlet's conditions Fourier series Euler's formulae Functions having points of discontinuity Change of interval Even and odd functions Half range series Harmonic analysis

UNIT IV

### Vector Calculus

8 hours

Vector differentiation Gradient, Divergence and Curl Directional derivative Solenoidal and Irrotational vector fields Vector Identities Line, Surface and Volume Integral Green's, Gauss & Stokes' Theorem

UNIT V

### Statistics and Probability

8 hours

Measures of Central Tendency Measures of Dispersion Moments, Skewness and Kurtosis Binomial, Poisson and Normal distributions

## Marks and credits

| Head | Marks | Credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theory: CCE | 40 | 3 |
| Theory: End-Semester | 60 | 3 |
| Tutorial / term work | 25 | 1 |

The prerequisites listed in the syllabus are integration, differential equations and three-dimensional coordinate systems. The course covers advanced integration, curve tracing, solid geometry, multiple integrals and their applications, and mathematical modelling of physical systems with differential equations. Term work is based on assignments on the units, with performance and continuous internal assessment.

## Course outcomes

1. CO1 Apply reduction formulae, Beta and Gamma functions, differentiation under the integral sign and error functions to evaluate integrals. Covers Unit I
2. CO2 Trace curves, measure arc length, and apply solid geometry to the sphere, cone and cylinder. Covers Unit II
3. CO3 Evaluate multiple integrals and use them for area, volume, centre of gravity and moment of inertia. Covers Unit III
4. CO4 Solve first order ordinary differential equations: exact, reducible to exact, linear and reducible to linear. Covers Unit IV
5. CO5 Model physical systems with ordinary differential equations: Newton’s law of cooling, electrical circuits, rectilinear motion, mass-spring systems and heat transfer. Covers Unit V

## Books

### Text books

- Higher Engineering Mathematics by B. V. Ramana (Tata McGraw Hill)
- Higher Engineering Mathematics by B. S. Grewal (Khanna Publication, Delhi)

### Reference books

- Advanced Engineering Mathematics by Erwin Kreyszig (Wiley Eastern Ltd.)
- Advanced Engineering Mathematics by M. D. Greenberg (Pearson Education)
- Advanced Engineering Mathematics by Peter V. O’Neil (Thomson Learning)
- Thomas’ Calculus by George B. Thomas (Addison-Wesley, Pearson)
- Applied Mathematics (Vol. I and II) by P. N. Wartikar and J. N. Wartikar (Vidyarthi Griha Prakashan, Pune)
- Differential Equations by S. L. Ross (John Wiley and Sons)

## Video lectures

The syllabus lists one playlist for this course, the same one it lists for Engineering Mathematics-I: [NPTEL / YouTube playlist](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLbRMhDVUMngeVrxtbBz-n8HvP8KAWBpI5).

Tick off each unit as you finish it, and keep your own notes and links in one place. It is free and needs no account.

[Open Engineering Mathematics-II in the app](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/#/subject/m2)

## FAQ

**How many credits is Engineering Mathematics-II in the SPPU 2024 pattern?**

BSC-151-BES carries 4 credits: 3 for theory (3 hours a week) and 1 for the tutorial (1 hour a week).

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-mathematics-2/#faq-1)

**How are the marks split?**

Theory is graded out of 100: CCE (continuous internal evaluation) 40 and End-Semester 60. Term work is a separate 25 marks tied to the tutorial credit.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-mathematics-2/#faq-2)

**How many units are there?**

Five units of 8 hours each, 40 hours in total: integral calculus, curve tracing and solid geometry, multiple integrals, first order ordinary differential equations, and applications of differential equations.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-mathematics-2/#faq-3)

**How is term work assessed?**

Through assignments on the units, based on performance and continuous internal assessment. The syllabus sets tutorial batches of at most 22 students.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-mathematics-2/#faq-4)

**Which books does the syllabus list?**

Text books: B. V. Ramana and B. S. Grewal, both titled Higher Engineering Mathematics. Six reference books are listed too, including Kreyszig, Thomas’ Calculus and S. L. Ross on differential equations.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/engineering-mathematics-2/#faq-5)

# Programming and Problem Solving syllabus

SPPU First Year Engineering, 2024 pattern, Semester II. Course code PCC-151-ITT. Five units of Python programming, 19 hours of theory and a practical component, with the marks scheme, outcomes and books taken from the official syllabus book.

3 credits (2 theory + 1 practical) CCE 40 + End-Sem 60 Term work 25 5 units, 19 hours

19 hours of theory

05 . units

03 . credits

## At a glance

Course codePCC-151-ITT

LevelFirst Year Engineering, SPPU 2024 pattern

Units5

Named topics17

Theory hours19

Credits3 (2 theory + 1 tutorial)

## Unit-wise syllabus

UNIT I

### Introduction to Computing and Programming

4 hours

Digital Computer & Computing Environment Computer Languages Problem Solving Programming Basics Elements of Python

UNIT II

### Control Structures

4 hours

Decision Making and Branching Loop Control Structures

UNIT III

### Functions and Modules

3 hours

Introduction to Functions User Defined Functions Parameters and Arguments Recursion Python Modules

UNIT IV

### Strings and List

4 hours

Strings: Introduction, Operations, Methods Lists: Introduction, Operations, Methods

UNIT V

### Tuples, Sets and Dictionaries

4 hours

Tuples: Introduction, Operations, Methods Sets: Introduction, Operations, Methods Dictionaries: Introduction, Operations, Methods

## Marks and credits

| Head | Marks | Credit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Theory: CCE | 40 | 2 |
| Theory: End-Semester | 60 | 2 |
| Practical / term work | 25 | 1 |

The prerequisites listed in the syllabus are basics of computers, basic mathematics and Fundamentals of Programming Languages. The course covers problem solving, then Python: data types, decision control, functions, strings, file handling and object oriented programming. The credit split follows the semester scheme table in the book (2 theory + 1 practical = 3); the course page itself prints a different practical figure, so check your college notice if it matters. The practical side has Group A assignments for each unit, and Group B assignments set by Mechanical, Civil and Electrical faculty in their own application domains.

## Course outcomes

1. CO1 Apply various skills in problem solving. Covers Unit I
2. CO2 Choose appropriate programming constructs and features to solve problems in different domains. Covers Unit II
3. CO3 Use functions and string manipulation for problem solving. Covers Unit III
4. CO4 Demonstrate file handling and dictionaries in Python. Covers Unit IV
5. CO5 Apply object oriented concepts in Python. Covers Unit V

## Books

### Text books

- Python Programming Using Problem Solving Approach by Reema Thareja (Oxford University Press)
- Core Python Programming by R. Nageswara Rao, 2nd edition (Dreamtech Press)

### Reference books

- How to Solve it by Computer by R. G. Dromey (Pearson Education India), and Problem Solving and Programming Concepts by Maureen Spankle (Pearson, 9th edition)
- Learning Python by Fabrizio Romano (Packt Publishing)
- Head First Python by Paul Barry, 2nd edition (SPD O’Reilly)
- Python: The Complete Reference by Martin C. Brown (McGraw Hill Education)
- Introduction to Computing and Problem Solving with Python by Jeeva Jose and P. Sojan Lal (Khanna Computer Book Store)

## Video lectures

The syllabus lists no NPTEL or video resources for this subject.

## Track it in PrepTracker

Tick off each unit as you finish it, and keep your own notes and links in one place. It is free and needs no account.

[Open Programming and Problem Solving in the app](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/#/subject/pps)

## FAQ

**How many credits is Programming and Problem Solving in the SPPU 2024 pattern?**

PCC-151-ITT carries 3 credits in the book’s semester scheme table: 2 for theory (2 hours a week) and 1 for practical (2 hours a week).

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/programming-and-problem-solving/#faq-1)

**How are the marks split?**

Theory is graded out of 100: CCE (continuous internal evaluation) 40 and End-Semester 60. Term work is a separate 25 marks tied to the practical credit.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/programming-and-problem-solving/#faq-2)

**Which language does the course use?**

Python. The five units cover problem solving and Python basics, advanced data types with decision control, functions and strings, file handling with dictionaries, and object oriented programming.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/programming-and-problem-solving/#faq-3)

**Is everything in the syllabus examined in theory?**

No. The Unit IV case study, on the design, features and use of a popular system built with Python, is excluded from the theory examination.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/programming-and-problem-solving/#faq-4)

**What are the lab assignments?**

Group A has practicals for each of the five units, from installing Python and operators to string operations, file handling and classes. Group B has assignments from Electrical, Mechanical and Civil application domains, designed with faculty from those branches.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/programming-and-problem-solving/#faq-5)

**Which books does the syllabus list?**

Two text books (Reema Thareja, and R. Nageswara Rao) and several reference books including Dromey, Fabrizio Romano’s Learning Python and Paul Barry’s Head First Python.

[Link to this answer](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/programming-and-problem-solving/#faq-6)

# SE Artificial Intelligence and Data Science syllabus

Second Year, SPPU 2024 pattern. Pick a subject for its units, marks, outcomes and books. Practical, lab and project courses are not listed here, only theory courses.

## Theory courses

[Data Structures PCC-201-AID · 3 cr](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/se-artificial-intelligence-and-data-science/data-structures/)

[Artificial Intelligence PCC-202-AID · 3 cr](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/se-artificial-intelligence-and-data-science/artificial-intelligence/)

[Operating System PCC-203-AID · 3 cr](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/se-artificial-intelligence-and-data-science/operating-system/)

[Digital Electronics and Logic Design MDM-221-AID · 2 cr](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/se-artificial-intelligence-and-data-science/digital-electronics-and-logic-design/)

# SE Cyber Security syllabus

Official PDF conflict: reference only.

The curriculum tables and detailed course pages in the same official 2024 PDF disagree. This page preserves the detailed theory-course text. Do not treat it as a confirmed semester plan; verify with your college.

- PCC-203: table says Basics of Computer Network; detailed page says Discrete Mathematics.
- MDM-221: table says Fundamentals of Internet of Things; detailed page says Digital Electronics and Logic Design.
- PCC-252: table says Discrete Mathematics; detailed page says Advanced Data Structures.
- PCC-253: table says Introduction to Cyber Security; detailed page says Probability and Statistics.
- MDM-271: table says Smart Devices and IoT Security; detailed page says Internet of Things.

PCC-202 is listed as theory in the table, but its detailed page has practical-only assessment. The replacement courses have no matching detailed units here. Tracking stays unavailable until a corrected source resolves this.

Second Year, SPPU 2024 pattern. Pick a subject for its units, marks, outcomes and books. Practical, lab and project courses are not listed here, only theory courses.

[Advanced Data Structures PCC-252-CYB · 3 cr](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/syllabus/se-cyber-security/advanced-data-structures/)

# Privacy policy

The short version: your study data never leaves your browser, there is no account, and analytics cookies run only if you accept them.

Last updated: 25 October 2026. PrepTracker is an independent student project, not affiliated with Savitribai Phule Pune University.

## Who we are

PrepTracker ([preptracker.manavdev.site](https://preptracker.manavdev.site/)) is an independent study planner for SPPU students. For anything in this policy, contact [sia@manavdev.site](mailto:sia@manavdev.site).

## What stays on your device

PrepTracker has no accounts and no server-side database. The following is stored only in your own browser's local storage:

- Study data: your profile, syllabus progress, tasks, marks, revision state and custom resources.
- Cookie choice: whether you accepted or rejected analytics cookies, so the banner does not keep asking.

- Backups are files you export yourself; they go only where you share or save them.
- Deleting everything: use the reset option in the app's Settings, or clear this site's data in your browser. Both remove every stored key.
- Switching browsers or devices starts fresh unless you restore a backup.

## Cookies and similar storage

This site uses two categories:

- Strictly necessary - the on-device storage described above. The site cannot function without it, so it is always on and is never sent to us.
- Analytics cookies - optional. They measure visit statistics: which pages are viewed, how long visits last, the approximate region (country or city level, worked out by the analytics provider), and the device and browser type. Visits are told apart by a random ID stored in the cookie, so the data is pseudonymous rather than anonymous. They are set only after you press Accept on the cookie banner, and advertising storage and ad personalization stay switched off.

Your choice is remembered on this device. To change it, use the Cookie settings button below to reset the banner, or clear this site's data in your browser.

## Error reports

If something breaks while you use the app or read the library, the site sends a short error report to an error-monitoring provider so the bug can be found and fixed. A report contains the error message, the page address, and your browser and operating system type. How long the monitoring provider keeps reports depends on its own settings and terms.

## Third parties that process data for this site

- Hosting and content delivery - serves the site's files and sees the technical data any web server sees (IP address, browser type, time of request), used to deliver pages and prevent abuse. It also runs a page-performance measurement script that sets no cookies.
- Font providers - the site's typefaces are loaded from external font services when a page opens, so these providers see your IP address, browser type and time of request. This happens before you make a cookie choice.
- Analytics provider - processes the pseudonymous visit statistics described above, only when you have accepted analytics cookies.
- Error-monitoring provider - receives the error reports described above.

Each provider processes only what its service needs, under its own privacy terms. Data may be processed on servers outside India; what safeguards apply is set out in each provider's own privacy terms and settings. How long each provider keeps data depends on its own settings and terms, which this policy does not fix.

## What PrepTracker does not do

- No accounts, sign-ups or passwords.
- No advertising, ad trackers, profiling or selling of data.
- No collection of names, emails, phone numbers or precise locations.
- No sharing of your on-device study data with anyone - it never reaches a server.

## Your rights

Most of your data never leaves your device, so you can exercise most rights directly: view or delete your stored study data and cookie choice at any time through the app's Settings or your browser settings.

India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 sets out rights to access, correct and erase personal data and to grievance redressal. Under the Government of India's notification of 13 November 2025, those provisions start 18 months after that date, so they are not yet in force. This page does not decide whether or how the Act applies to this site. To ask about your data, such as the analytics and error data described above, email [sia@manavdev.site](mailto:sia@manavdev.site).

## Children

PrepTracker is a general study tool and does not knowingly collect personal data from children. Since there are no accounts and analytics is opt-in, no age-specific data is gathered.

## Changes to this policy

If this policy changes, the "last updated" date at the top changes with it. Material changes are also flagged in the app for a reasonable time.

## Contact and grievances

Questions, requests or complaints: [sia@manavdev.site](mailto:sia@manavdev.site). The Data Protection Board of India is set up under the Act, but its complaint provisions are not yet in force.

---

PrepTracker is an independent student project and is not affiliated with Savitribai Phule Pune University.
